title: Ticket revenue decline and a contract decision at the Tarrant Valley Symphony Orchestra

organization.size: operating budget approx. $6.8M; 74 contracted musicians, 31 administrative staff; 30-32 subscription concerts per season

presentingRequest: Our ticket revenue has fallen 30% in three seasons. The music director's programming has drifted toward music our audience doesn't want, and the marketing she is supposed to champion is invisible. The board will vote in December on whether to renew her contract, which expires on 30 June 2027. We want an independent view that confirms what is driving the decline and a recommendation we can act on at that meeting. - Gordon Pryce, Board Chair

evidence.text: 'Ticket revenue was $2.41 million in 2022-23 and $1.69 million last season. That's a 30% collapse on Dr. Marek's watch. She keeps putting Ligeti and new commissions in front of people who came for Beethoven and Brahms. And nobody in Westmere knows when we're playing; the marketing is invisible. The hall renovation is no excuse: people travel for music they want to hear. I want a recommendation for the December 9 board meeting, and my view is that we should not renew her and start a search.'

evidence.source: Finance office, ticket revenue summary by season (audited figures to 2024-25; 2025-26 management accounts)
evidence.text: Season / concerts / tickets sold / average tickets per concert / average price / ticket revenue: 2021-22: 32 / 50,300 / 1,572 / $45.20 / $2.275M. 2022-23: 32 / 51,520 / 1,610 / $46.80 / $2.411M. 2023-24: 30 / 34,500 / 1,150 / $50.00 / $1.725M (-28.5% vs prior season). 2024-25: 30 / 32,400 / 1,080 / $54.00 / $1.750M (+1.4%). 2025-26: 30 / 31,200 / 1,040 / $54.20 / $1.691M (-3.4%). Cumulative 2022-23 to 2025-26: -29.9%. Average prices were raised in 2023-24 and again in 2024-25 'to offset reduced seating capacity' (finance note).

evidence.source: Board member Henrietta Vos, compiled patron correspondence and press (memo to board, 2026-09-15)
evidence.text: Memo attaches 46 patron emails received in 2024-25 objecting to 'modern' or 'difficult' works (9 emails praising the same programs are listed in an appendix). Also attaches a Westmere Ledger column (2025-03-22) headlined 'Marek's adventurous seasons are emptying seats', which cites the drop in attendance since 2022-23 but no data on individual concerts. Memo concludes: 'The pattern is clear - the repertoire is driving people away.'

evidence.source: Ticketing system export, tickets by buyer type and subscriber households (2022-23 to 2025-26)
evidence.text: Subscription tickets / single tickets / subscriber households: 2022-23: 23,420 / 28,100 / 3,950. 2023-24: 19,100 / 15,400 / 3,420. 2024-25: 17,800 / 14,600 / 3,310. 2025-26: 17,000 / 14,200 / 3,260. Single-ticket sales fell 45% between 2022-23 and 2023-24 and a further 8% over the following two seasons combined.

evidence.source: Patron CRM, subscriber renewal analysis by attendance (development office analyst)
evidence.text: Renewal rate into the next season for subscriber households that scanned tickets at 3 or more concerts in the season: 2022-23 86%, 2023-24 85%, 2024-25 86%, 2025-26 85% (renewals for 2026-27 as of 2026-11-10, campaign closed). For households that scanned tickets at 0-2 concerts: 60%, 43%, 46%, 44%. Share of subscriber households in the 0-2 group: 2022-23 14%, 2023-24 29%, 2024-25 28%, 2025-26 27%.

evidence.source: Artistic planning archive, repertoire composition by season
evidence.text: Share of program minutes devoted to works composed after 1945: 2021-22 17%, 2022-23 18%, 2023-24 21%, 2024-25 27%, 2025-26 31%. Commissions/premieres per season: 1, 2, 2, 3, 3. Dr. Ilona Marek has been music director since the 2021-22 season.

evidence.source: Ticketing analyst, per-concert sales at the Brightwater venue, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (56 concerts)
evidence.text: Concerts whose program included at least one post-1945 work of 15 minutes or longer (n=31): average 1,034 tickets sold; 5 sell-outs. Concerts without such a work (n=25): average 1,019 tickets sold; 4 sell-outs. Same venue, same price bands, same day-of-week mix (analyst note). Pops and holiday concerts are excluded from both groups.

evidence.source: Current-patron survey, October 2025 (n=1,312 ticket buyers from 2024-25)
evidence.text: Satisfaction with programming: 58% satisfied, 19% neutral, 23% dissatisfied. Preferred direction: 41% 'more familiar classics', 24% 'more new or lesser-known works', 35% 'current balance is about right'. Among respondents who said they attended less often than three years earlier, 'programming' was named as a reason by 12% and 'getting to the venue / travel' by 47% (multiple answers allowed).

evidence.source: Operations director, venue and facilities summary (document, 2026-10)
evidence.text: Castellan Hall (2,150 seats, downtown, 250 m from Central rail station) closed on 2023-06-01 for a city-led renovation. Reopening was scheduled for September 2026; in March 2026 the city announced a contractor delay to September 2027. Since 2023-24 subscription concerts have been held at the Brightwater Convention Centre auditorium (1,290 sellable seats, 40% fewer), 6.5 km from downtown. Nearest rail stop 2.4 km away; evening bus every 45 minutes, last departure 22:10, while concerts typically end around 22:15. On-site parking $24 per evening.

evidence.source: Regional Orchestra League, benchmarking report for member orchestras (August 2026)
evidence.text: Six comparable regional orchestras (budgets $4-9M), none of which changed venue in 2022-26. Ticket revenue change 2022-23 to 2025-26: range -25% to -35%, median -29%. Median year-on-year change: 2023-24 -8%, 2024-25 -11%, 2025-26 -12%. Median single-ticket volume change 2022-23 to 2023-24: -9%. Median average-price change 2022-23 to 2025-26: +14%. Median ticket revenue change 2021-22 to 2022-23: +1%. Report attributes the regional decline to an ageing subscriber base, cost-of-living pressure and changed post-2020 attendance habits.

evidence.source: Ticketing system and finance, downtown concerts at St. Aldric Cathedral (4 concerts, 2024-25 and 2025-26)
evidence.text: Because of Brightwater booking conflicts, two subscription programs per season were moved to St. Aldric Cathedral (1,650 sellable seats, 300 m from Central rail station), with the same price bands as Brightwater. Two of the four programs included a post-1945 work over 15 minutes. Average tickets sold: 1,520 (vs 1,027 at Brightwater over the same two seasons). Single-ticket buyers were 58% of cathedral sales vs 34% at Brightwater. Net contribution per concert after the higher rental and staging costs: about $31,000 above the Brightwater average. The cathedral has offered six dates in 2026-27.

evidence.source: Lapsed-patron exit survey, March 2026 (640 respondents; 22% response rate)
evidence.text: Sample: single-ticket buyers who bought at least twice in 2021-23 but not since 2024, plus non-renewing subscribers. Main reason for stopping (one answer): travel/transit to Brightwater 41%; parking cost or late-night safety 17%; smaller hall or could not get preferred seats 9%; programming 11%; ticket prices 8%; health/age 8%; other 6%. 71% said they would 'likely' or 'very likely' return when concerts are back downtown.

evidence.source: Governance file: organization chart and music director employment agreement (2021)
evidence.text: The marketing and communications department (director plus 4 staff) reports to the Executive Director, not to the music director. The music director's agreement assigns her artistic programming, conducting 14-18 concerts per season, and artistic personnel decisions; it lists 'participation in donor and community events' but no marketing responsibilities. Contract term ends 30 June 2027; the board must give notice of non-renewal by 31 December 2026.

'The building is the story. We lost 860 seats and a downtown location overnight. We raised prices twice to protect revenue per seat; honestly I can't tell you whether that cost us buyers, because the hall changed at the same time. On marketing: the director's post was vacant from June to September 2024, and we have never tracked which campaign or channel sells which tickets, so I can't prove the marketing is good or bad.'

Halvorsen Family Foundation artistic-excellence grant: $1.2M over 2025-26 to 2027-28 ($400,000 per season). Clause 7 (key person): if Dr. Ilona Marek ceases to be music director, unpaid installments lapse. State Arts Council New Works grant: $180,000 per season, conditional on at least two commissions or premieres per season.

evidence.source: Marketing Director, Kwame Osei (interview, 2026-11-04; in post since September 2024)
evidence.text: 'Marketing spend has been roughly flat: $310k, $318k, $305k and $322k for the last four seasons. Campaign creative and media buying have been handled by the same outside agency throughout. We shifted about a third of print spend to digital in 2025-26. Email open rates and web sessions are in the ranges I'd expect, but without attribution I cannot tell you which campaigns sold tickets or whether a different mix would have sold more.'

hypotheses.text: The music director's programming choices are the main cause of the 30% decline in ticket revenue.
The size of the decline is not unusual for the region: comparable orchestras lost a similar share of ticket revenue over the same seasons.
The move to the smaller, less accessible temporary venue caused a large drop in attendance by single-ticket buyers and low-usage subscribers.
Ineffective marketing materially contributed to the decline in ticket revenue.
The orchestra's committed core audience is defecting because of dissatisfaction with the artistic direction.
Had the orchestra stayed in Castellan Hall, its ticket revenue would have fallen far less than 30% over the three seasons.

edges.from: Relocation of subscription concerts to the Brightwater venue (from 2023-24)
Rising share of post-1945 works in the programming
Average ticket price increases in 2023-24 and 2024-25

actions.text: At the December 2026 meeting, give notice that the music director's contract will not be renewed, citing the ticket-revenue decline, and start a search.

Before the contract decision, present the board with a segmented analysis of the decline (buyer type, peer benchmark, venue comparison, per-concert repertoire comparison) and separate the artistic review from the revenue question.
For the remaining interim season, take up the cathedral's six downtown dates for high-demand programs and pilot a post-concert shuttle from Brightwater to Central rail station.
Replace the marketing agency and restructure the marketing team before the 2026-27 single-ticket campaign.
Reduce post-1945 works to under 10% of program minutes and drop commissions for 2026-27 to win back audiences.

evidenceRequests.text: Campaign- and channel-level marketing attribution data, 2022-23 to 2025-26
Peer orchestras' attendance by buyer segment and seat capacity, 2021-22 to 2025-26
Postcode-level travel-time analysis of lapsed versus retained patrons
Music director's recording, touring and guest-conducting history
Musicians' rehearsal attendance and sick-leave records, 2022-26
Advance sales to date for the 2026-27 season by concert
